content:
I fully admit my DIY iPhone camera mod looks pretty ridiculous—but it has actually made using my iPhone for photos more practical and more fun.

It started as a one-off fix for a specific video shoot, but ended up being something I reach for far more often than I ever expected…

One of the biggest divides in the compact camera world is whether or not a camera has a viewfinder. Once upon a time, camera enthusiasts were fiercely divided over electronic viewfinders (EVF) versus optical ones, but EVFs have become so good now that almost nobody cares anymore.

But whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder offers a very practical advantage over composing with the rear screen—especially when shooting in harsh sunlight. Even at maximum brightness, the screen is almost impossible to see clearly when the sun is blazing down, and you also have to deal with reflections.

Here in London, this hasn't historically been a huge problem, but this summer has brought record-breaking heatwaves, and honestly it feels like the last time I saw a cloud or any rain was roughly three centuries ago.

But for me, it goes beyond that. I also feel there's something psychologically different about seeing only what's in the frame versus being able to see everything around it. Sometimes it's exactly that feeling that makes me prefer to use a dedicated camera rather than my iPhone.

When I was choosing a camcorder a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was clearly the hot pick, but the lack of a viewfinder gave me pause at the time. In the end, I decided it wasn't a dealbreaker for me, because I'd mainly be using it indoors, and for the occasions I needed it outside, adding a big screen with a sun hood solved most of the problem.

However, sometimes I want something even more portable and don't want to haul the whole rig with the monitor out on the street, so I found a simple accessory that's great for outdoor use. It's a sun hood combined with a magnifying lens that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, effectively giving you an optical viewfinder.

I had an upcoming shoot where I'd be using both the BMPCC 4K and an iPhone 16 Pro Max for video. I did a quick test on location and found the viewfinder accessory genuinely helpful. The screen sizes of the BMPCC 4K and iPhone are very similar, so I wondered if this accessory would work on the iPhone.

Of course, the iPhone doesn't have a magnetic attachment feature, but the iPhone is light enough that just holding it up against the magnifying lens isn't an issue at all. To my surprise, it worked remarkably well, especially when using the Camera Control button as the shutter.

After that, I found myself reaching for it in all sorts of shooting situations, not just because it makes the screen easier to see in harsh sunlight, but also because it gives you a more immersive feel. My iPhone became my main camera a few years ago, and with this DIY mod, I find that more often than not, just bringing my phone is enough.

Crazy or genius? Let me know your take in the comments. If it's the latter, apologies—the item I bought seems to have been discontinued, and I haven't yet found a similar product specifically designed for screens larger than three inches. If you come across one, drop a link in the comments.
